about: Coach-facing wording Christian has APPROVED for parts of a game the renderer otherwise cannot say: primary-event conditions (register V4-V6) and information rules (V16-V22), and later the modifier criterion and termination (V8c, V8d). His order of 14 October 2026, Step 4 component 3: 'Enable accurate coach-facing communication of scoring conditions and information rules, using approved language.' An entry is used only when it carries approvedBy with who, a date, his words verbatim and the communication standard it was reviewed under; the loader ignores any other entry and a data test fails it. Wording is data, so no sport term enters universal code. Starts EMPTY on 14 October 2026: until he approves a sentence, every such field is withheld and the activity is refused at communication rather than paraphrased.

entryShape.id: a stable id for the entry
entryShape.covers: [{ row: 'V3' (a condition's scope)|'V4'|'V5'|'V6'|'V8c'|'V8d'|'V16'..'V22'|'B8' (a role's credit bound)|'V28'..'V31' (an occurrence that also counts as the primary event), match: { equals: <JSON value> } | { refersToOwnCondition: true }, element?: { base: '<a collection said only in approved words, e.g. activityRoles or value.primaryEvent.conditions>', field: '<a field of its elements>', equals: <JSON value> } }] - without `element`, every cover must hold on one element for the entry to apply, and it is said once per such element; with `element` on EVERY cover (stage M3, 17 October 2026), each locator must pick out exactly one element, every cover must hold on its own element, a located condition authored for less than every score needs its exact V3 cover, and the sentence is said ONCE citing every covered field (no slots); equality is canonical JSON, key order ignored (documentation only; the rows said only in approved words are render-concrete-game.ts WORDED_ONLY; B8 and V28-V31 listed 17 October 2026, stages M1 and M2)
entryShape.sentence: the approved sentence; {slot} names a slot
entryShape.slots: { slotName: { field: '<field of the same element>' } } - filled only from cited game values
entryShape.section: Set up | Players | How it works | How to score | What to watch

templateShape.note: Added 17 October 2026 (stage M4) for his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 4. A sentence he approved for a template the renderer already says - fields it may say on its own, so not an entry above (which holds wording only for fields said in approved words). Read by approved-wording.ts approvedTemplateSentences(): usable only where it carries approvedBy as an entry does, his sentence is verbatim inside the quote, and its parts filled with the example values reproduce his sentence exactly (a final full stop aside). Filled with any other value it is a generalization of his words, DRAFT.
templateShape.id: the name the renderer reads it by (render-concrete-game.ts); never words
templateShape.renders: what it says and where the renderer says it
templateShape.parts: the renderer's parts, in order; {slot} names a slot filled from a cited game value

approvedTemplateSentences.renders: A game whose transition keyed on a change of possession continues play, with one objective per team: the first part cites each such transition's play state and selector, the second the objectives' team and the targets' noun (render-concrete-game.ts, 'How it works'). The second part is said only where the two objectives name different teams; targetNoun is the referenced regions' one noun, and 'line' where they name no other.
parts: When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage
, and each team keeps attacking the same {targetNoun}
approvedTemplateSentences.sentence: When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage, and each team keeps attacking the same zone.

approvedBy.quote: I approve both of your proposed revisions: … Use: "When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage, and each team keeps attacking the same zone." For the second sentence, please ensure the surrounding scoring instructions make clear that continuing to attack does not automatically restore the building team's eligibility to score.
approvedBy.ccs: Coach Communication Standard RC2: our draft, section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026, which put every sentence to him as a draft
